name: Μάναγρος
evidence: The SE section named Managros itself has no umbrellas/sunbeds; only the adjacent Gonia section has a beach bar/cafe with loungers.

name: Κατσούνι
evidence: No source specific to Katsouni on Psara found; results collide with Katsouni beaches on Rhodes and Anafi.

name: Κακοπετριά
evidence: Oinousses guide states the pebble beach just outside the settlement has umbrellas protecting visitors, with shops/tavernas nearby (no beach bar mentioned).

name: Νας
evidence: Visit Ikaria and travel guides explicitly say Nas is not organized; tavernas are up on the cliff, and strong currents warrant caution.

name: Φύτεμα
evidence: No specific source found for Fytema; Ikaria organized-beach lists (Mesakti, Livadi, Kampos, Gialiskari) do not include it.

name: Αμμουδέλι
evidence: Lesvos beach guide: the small sandy beach 300m from Plomari square is organized with umbrellas and sun loungers and quite popular.

name: Αυλάκι
evidence: No source specific to Avlaki on Lesvos found; name collides with Avlaki in Attica and Corfu.

name: Παραλία Άναξου
evidence: Visit Lesvos: Anaxos is a Blue Flag sandy beach with modern organization — recliner chairs, umbrellas, changing booths, showers — plus beach bars and water sports.

name: Παραλία Γυμνιστών Χρούσος
evidence: travel.gr describes Chrousos (W Lesvos, dirt-road access) as an unorganized beach with tavernas nearby; the nudist section is part of this wild beach.

name: Παραλία Δρότας
evidence: A taverna ("Drota", since 2017) sits on the beach, but no source states sunbeds/umbrellas; described as a quiet natural pebble beach.

name: Παραλία Καγιά
evidence: Kagia near Skala Sikamnias has a fish taverna at the beach but is described as a natural, undeveloped pebble beach; no explicit sunbed/organization statement found.

name: Παραλία Νυφίδας
evidence: Visit Lesvos: Nyfida has fine organization with showers, changing booths, umbrellas, recliner beach chairs; tavernas and refreshment stands along the seafront.

name: Παραλία Τάρτι
evidence: lesvosbeaches.gr: at Tarti you'll find sunbeds, umbrellas and a beach bar, plus tavernas overlooking the beach.

name: Πλαζ Κανόνι
evidence: Kanoni at Thermi is an organized Blue Flag beach with recliner chairs, umbrellas, showers, changing booths, and beach bars/tavernas.

name: Τσιχράντα
evidence: Visit Lesvos describes Mikri/Megali Tsichranta as small idyllic coves ideal for isolation and quiet swimming; no facilities mentioned but no explicit 'unorganized' statement.

name: Φαρά
evidence: Wikipedia (Blue Flag 2025): in summer a canteen operates at Fara offering free loungers and shade under mastic trees.

name: Χαλατσές
evidence: Official bathing water profile: not formally organized but has showers, changing rooms, umbrellas and loungers plus a refreshment stand on the beach.

name: Χρούσος
evidence: travel.gr: Chrousos is an unorganized 1.5km sandy beach reached by 4km dirt road, with tavernas nearby only.

name: Μπάλος
evidence: Conflicting: samosin.gr says Balos (SW Samos) is not organized with tavernas by the road, while the bathing water profile says a section has umbrellas/loungers.

name: Μικρά Λεμονάκια
evidence: Searches only return the main Lemonakia beach (organized); could not disambiguate a distinct 'Mikra Lemonakia' cove, so no beach-specific evidence.

name: Λεμονάκια
evidence: Lemonakia near Kokkari is organized with umbrellas and loungers for rent, a beach bar, changing rooms, shower and a beachfront restaurant.

name: Διαπόρι (δυτική ακτή)
evidence: Terrabook/limnos.mobi: Diapori (Kontias bay, near Tsimandria) has no organized section with umbrellas/sunbeds, only a small taverna.

name: Άγιος Ιωάννης
evidence: Agios Ioannis Kaspakas (Blue Flag) is fully organized with umbrellas and loungers and a beach bar, with free space for own equipment.

name: Διαπόρι (ανατολική ακτή)
evidence: Same Diapori beach area: no organized umbrellas/sunbeds section, only a small taverna by the anchorage.

name: Παραλία Κότσινα
evidence: Kotsinas beach is fully organized with umbrellas, sunbeds and a beach bar; picturesque tavernas nearby.

name: Γκλιάτη
evidence: Gliati/Kalymnios (Palaia Epidavros) is an unorganized beach with no facilities — visitors must bring umbrellas, mats and water.

name: Καλαμάκι
evidence: Kalamaki near Vagionia (Ancient Epidavros), reached on foot through the pine wood, has no infrastructure — no sunbeds available.

name: Μπούκα
evidence: All 'Bouka organized' evidence refers to Bouka in Messinia (Messiniakos Gulf), not the Argolida beach; no Argolida-specific source found.

name: Παραλία Ασίνης
evidence: Ancient Asini beach next to Tolo is organized with a cafe, sunbeds, rental umbrellas and showers.

name: Παραλία Βαγιωνία
evidence: Conflicting: one source says only a few straw umbrellas and no loungers, another (pocket-guide) calls it organized with sunbeds, umbrellas and a cafe snack bar.

name: Παραλία Κάντιας
evidence: Kantia beach (Argolida) is very well organized with sun loungers, beach bars, tavernas, showers and free parking along its length.

name: Παραλία Κιβερίου
evidence: Kiveri beach is organized with sunbeds, umbrellas, showers, changing rooms; cafes and tavernas serve the beach.

name: Παραλία Μύλων
evidence: Myloi beach is organized with bather facilities — umbrellas, showers, changing rooms, bins; seafront tavernas and cafes in the village.

name: Ζαρίτσι
evidence: Zaritsi (Tyros) is partially organized with beach bars for coffee/drinks and tavernas; the organized Zaritsi Camping operates beside it.

name: Κρυονέρι
evidence: Kryoneri (S Kynouria) is an organized pebble beach with a canteen providing loungers, toilets and showers; cafeterias on the main road manage loungers and umbrellas.

name: Παραλία Βερβένων
evidence: Kato Vervena / Paliochano beach: a canteen mid-beach offers plenty of loungers and umbrellas, with ample free space for own equipment.

name: Πούλιθρα
evidence: Poulithra's pebble beach is partly organized — sunbeds available on a section of the beach, with tavernas along the shore.

name: Παραλία Μυλοκοπή
evidence: Mylokopi (Corinthian Gulf, near Lake Vouliagmeni) is explicitly not organized — no canteens, umbrellas, sunbeds or beach bar.

name: Παραλία Σκαλωσιά
evidence: Skalosia near Loutraki is not organized — visitors must bring water, food and umbrella; access via stone stairs.
